title: What Your Net Worth Should Be at Every Age (And What to Do If It Isn't)
description:
What should your net worth be at 25, 35, 45, 55 and 65? I use Federal Reserve data to show the real medians at every age, what they hide, and a catch up plan if you're behind.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:36 How we got the numbers
2:25 Angle 1: The numbers
4:36 Under 35
6:17 Age 35 to 44
7:50 Age 45 to 54
9:36 Age 55 to 64
11:10 Age 65 and up
12:41 What really moves net worth
15:11 Five people, five decades
17:50 Angle 2: The psychology
20:49 Angle 3: The catch up playbook
23:09 The biggest mistake in each decade
25:14 The ten year challenge
26:56 Questions people ask
30:02 Recap: net worth by age
31:33 What to do next

Sources:
- Federal Reserve, Changes in U.S. Family Finances from 2019 to 2022: Evidence from the Survey of Consumer Finances (median net worth all families $192,700, mean $1,063,700; by age of head: under 35 $39,040; 35-44 $135,300; 45-54 $246,700; 55-64 $364,500; 65-74 $409,900; 75+ $335,600)
- Fidelity Investments, How much do I need to save for retirement? (1x salary by 30, 3x by 40, 6x by 50, 8x by 60, 10x by 67)
- Thomas J. Stanley and William D. Danko, The Millionaire Next Door (1996) (expected net worth = age x pretax income / 10)
- IRS, catch-up contributions and required minimum distributions (check current-year rules)
- Social Security Administration, delayed retirement credits (benefits grow for each year of delay up to age 70)
- FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center, Elder Fraud Report
- Compound growth: stated illustrative math at 7% average yearly return, compounded monthly

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video07.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
